title: Is the News Too Negative?
blurb: Talk about news and how it's reported

steps.html:
Ugly vegetables sold at a discount. A monkey nobody had recorded before. Two teenagers who found eighty thousand dollars on a train and handed it in. Three stories that are news, and would not normally be reported.

  • Follow three news stories and take the detail from them
  • Choose the right reporting verb, and the right pattern after it
  • Talk about how news gets selected
  • Write a short news report

steps.title: Why is most news bad news?

options.label: People pay more attention to threats
Good things happen slowly and are hard to report
It is not true — the news is balanced

steps.title: Make a guess.
steps.prompt: A French supermarket chain sold misshapen fruit and vegetables at a discount. What happened?
options: The campaign failed and was withdrawn
Everything sold out within three days
Customers said the food tasted worse
steps.answer: Everything sold out within three days
steps.why: And in blind tastings the customers admitted they could not tell the difference.

steps.title: Study the words.
steps.sub: Twelve items. The first four are reporting verbs — the pattern after each one matters as much as the meaning.

words.def: To agree, reluctantly, that something is true. Admit doing or admit that — never an infinitive.
To give reasons for a position. Argue that.
To tell somebody firmly that something is true, so that they worry less. Needs a person.
To show or suggest something without stating it directly.
Stealing from a person or place using a weapon.
A formal arrangement to end a conflict.
Giving you hope that something will improve.
Making you feel happier and more hopeful.
Success in a struggle, a competition or an argument.
An organised effort to protect the natural world.
Someone who works to protect wildlife or the environment.

steps.title: Read between the lines.
steps.sub: All three stories are true, recent and reported — and none of them led the news.
steps.prompt: What does the selection of these three suggest about news values?
options: That editors are actively hostile to good news of any kind.
That an event needs more than being true and recent to be reported prominently, and the missing ingredient is usually conflict.
That positive stories take longer to verify than negative ones.
steps.answer: That an event needs more than being true and recent to be reported prominently, and the missing ingredient is usually conflict.
steps.why: A discovery, an act of honesty and a successful campaign all lack a villain. That is the property they share.

steps.title: The verb, and the pattern it takes
steps.html:
Not just say and tell — the verbs that report and evaluate at the same time.

A reporting verb does two jobs: it says what was said, and it tells the reader what you think of it. He claimed the campaign worked and He confirmed the campaign worked report the same words and take opposite positions on them.

The patterns are fixed and have to be learned with the verb.

+ that clause: admit, argue, announce, claim, confirm, deny, explain, insist, point out, reply, report, suggest. She argued that it was manufactured.

+ -ing: admit, deny, report, suggest, recommend. Hunters reported seeing an unusual monkey.

+ person + that clause: tell, assure, inform, remind, persuade, warn. These need a person. He assured me that…, never He assured that…

+ person + to + infinitive: advise, invite, persuade, remind, warn, ask, tell. They invited him to comment.

+ to + infinitive, no person: refuse, offer, promise, agree, threaten. He refused to comment.

The trap: suggest and recommend never take a person plus infinitive. She suggested selling them or She suggested that they sell them, never She suggested them to sell.

steps.title: Example bank.
steps.html:
Twelve sentences from the three stories.

The supermarket claims that the campaign was a success.
Claim = states it, without proof.

Customers admitted that they tasted exactly the same.
Admit = agreed reluctantly.

The supermarket has announced it will continue the campaign.
That can be dropped.

The teenagers pointed out that the cash wasn't theirs.
Point out = drew attention to a fact.

Hunters reported seeing a monkey unlike any they knew.
Report + -ing.

Conservationists confirmed that it was a new species.
Confirm = it was already reported and is true.

He denied taking the bag.
Deny + -ing — never an infinitive.

He assured me that he would return it.
Assure needs a person.

They reminded him to hand it in.
Person + infinitive.

He refused to comment.
Infinitive, no person.

She suggested selling them at a discount.
-ing, never a person plus infinitive.

Critics insisted that it was only publicity.
Insist = repeated it against opposition.

steps.title: Choosing the verb, then the pattern
steps.html:
1. The words: 'The campaign was a success.' — said by the supermarket.
  2. First decide what you think of it. If you accept it: confirmed. If you are reporting it neutrally: said, announced, reported. If you doubt it: claimed. The verb carries your position.
  3. Now take the pattern. Claim takes a that clause: The supermarket claimed that the campaign had been a success.
  4. Change the verb and the pattern may change with it. Report also takes -ing: The supermarket reported selling out within three days.
  5. And watch the ones that need a person. They assured customers that the discount would continue — remove customers and the sentence is wrong.

steps.title: You are going to write a short news report.

options.label: A good-news story from where you live
One of the three stories in this lesson, in your own words
Something that happened at your work or school
A story you think was reported unfairly

steps.title: Write your report.
steps.sub: 140–170 words. Use at least five different reporting verbs, with the right pattern after each.
steps.html:
• Open with an announcement, using <i>has announced that</i>.
  • Give the two sides, using <i>claims that</i> and <i>argue that</i>.
  • Include one verb that needs a person: <i>assured</i>, <i>reminded</i>, <i>invited</i>.
  • Include one concession, using <i>admitted</i>.
  • Close with somebody who <i>refused to</i> do something.

Useful language

  • … has announced that …
  • The company claims that … , although critics argue that …
  • Those involved admitted …-ing
  • A spokesperson assured residents that …
  • He refused to comment.
  • Conservationists have confirmed that …
steps.modelHtml:
Bus shelter returned after eleven months

The city council has announced that the bus shelter on Erzhanov Street will be reinstalled next month, eleven months after it was removed for repair.

The council claims that the delay was caused by a supply problem. Residents argue that the shelter was simply forgotten, and point out that three separate letters received no reply at all.

A spokesperson has now assured residents that the work will be finished before November. She admitted that the communication had been poor, and confirmed that the same design will be used.

One resident, who has waited at the stop every working morning since October, refused to comment beyond saying that she would believe it when she saw it.

The council has invited residents to report any other missing shelters.
